title: Freedom and cash plan (editable template)
audience: Owners or prospective owners who want to turn a personal income goal into a monthly money target and a weekly hours check
learningOutcomes: Separate personal costs, business costs and the tax set-aside into three totals
Calculate break-even jobs per month from contribution per job, not gross job value
Check whether the required jobs fit within the weekly hours available, including non-billable time

instruction.heading: Why this plan starts from your life
instruction.body: The freedom number from the earlier lesson states what you want your life to cost. This template turns that into money: what you spend each month, what the business has to take in after its costs, and how many billable hours that needs. Many operators underestimate the hours that do not earn money, such as travel, quoting, bookkeeping and rework. Include them as their own line. A plan that leaves them out can look achievable on paper and then fail in the first month of trading.

instruction.heading: Separating personal costs, business costs and the set-aside
instruction.body: Keep three lists apart. Personal costs are what you spend to live. Business costs are what the business spends to operate, which can include vehicle running costs, tools, consumables not charged to customers, insurance, phone and software, and bank fees. The set-aside is money held back for tax and any other obligation you carry. This template does not tell you what rate to use. Add a cash buffer expressed as a number of months, so that a slow month does not force a price cut.

instruction.heading: Working out break-even jobs and the hours check
instruction.body: Add the cash buffer to the monthly target, then divide the total by the contribution each job makes after its materials and travel. The result is the number of jobs needed per month, rounded up to a whole job. Then test the hours. Jobs multiplied by the hours per job, plus the non-billable hours, must fit inside the hours you can work each week. If they do not fit, the plan needs a higher contribution per job, lower fixed costs, a different target or more hours. Seeing that before you start is far cheaper than discovering it after you have taken on customers.

procedure: List the monthly personal costs in the table and total them.
List the monthly business costs in the table and total them separately.
Enter the set-aside and the cash buffer as your own figures, recording where each figure came from or leaving it blank.
Set the monthly income target as personal costs plus business costs plus the set-aside plus the buffer contribution.
Enter the average job value, then the materials and travel per job, and calculate the contribution per job.
Divide the monthly income target by the contribution per job to get break-even jobs per month, rounded up.
Enter the weekly hours you can work and the non-billable hours, then compare the hours needed with the hours available.
Record the decision taken after the hours check: a change to price, volume, cost or target, with the reason and the date.
Save the template with the date, and complete the checklist.

workedExamples.situation: A solo operator wants a monthly income target that covers personal costs, business costs, a set-aside and a buffer. The operator estimates that travel and quoting take about a third of the working week.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: The break-even result needs more jobs per week than the operator can physically do. What are the options, and which single option should the plan record?
workedExamples.reasoning: Three options are open: raise the contribution per job by changing the price, reduce the fixed costs, or change the target by changing the lifestyle costs or the timing of the buffer. The plan should record one chosen option, with the reason and the date, not a list of hopes. This example uses no figures; the operator enters their own. The key point is that the hours check comes before any decision about extra work, hiring or price, and the decision is written down so it can be reviewed.

equipmentAndPpe: Freedom number from the earlier lesson
Recent bank or accounting records for the business, if available
PPE: not applicable to this lesson

commonErrors.error: Leaving out non-billable time such as travel, quoting and admin.
commonErrors.prevention: Enter those hours as their own line and include them in the hours check.

commonErrors.error: Treating the tax set-aside as optional or as a guessed percentage.
commonErrors.prevention: Record the source of the figure, or leave it blank and get advice before trading.

commonErrors.error: Dividing the target by job value rather than by contribution per job.
commonErrors.prevention: Subtract materials, travel and other per-job costs before dividing.

commonErrors.error: Forgetting that the buffer must also be earned.
commonErrors.prevention: Add the buffer contribution to the target before dividing by contribution per job.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Tax, superannuation and insurance obligations depend on how the business is set up and on the work it does. This template does not state them. Confirm with a registered tax agent or another qualified adviser.
Working long hours to reach a target increases fatigue, and fatigue increases the risk of driving incidents and injury on site. Build rest days and travel time into the hours check.

qualityStandard: Personal, business and set-aside costs are listed separately and totalled
Break-even jobs are calculated from contribution per job, not from gross job value
The hours check includes non-billable time and shows whether the plan fits the week
Any change to price, volume or costs is recorded with a reason and a date
documentationEvidence: Completed freedom and cash template with calculations visible
Source of the set-aside and insurance figures, or a blank field with the adviser to be consulted
Signed decision record for any change made after the hours check
summary: Start from the life you want and work back to money and hours.
Non-billable time is part of the cost of running the business.
Break-even is a number of jobs, and those jobs must fit in the hours you can work.
Leave out every figure you have not confirmed.

editableTemplates.title: Freedom and cash plan
editableTemplates.purpose: Converts a personal income goal into a monthly target, a break-even job count and a weekly hours check, and records the decision taken.

fields.label: Personal monthly costs
fields.prompt: One row per cost. Columns: cost item, monthly amount, notes. Total at the bottom.
fields.guidance: Covers housing, food, private transport, health, insurance, debt repayments and the costs of any dependants. Each row shows its basis.

fields.label: Business monthly costs
fields.prompt: One row per cost. Columns: cost item, monthly amount, notes. Total at the bottom.
fields.guidance: Covers business use of the vehicle, tools and replacement, consumables not charged to customers, business insurance, phone, software and bank fees. Unconfirmed costs are left out.

fields.label: Tax and obligation set-aside per month
fields.prompt: Enter your own monthly figure and where it came from.
fields.guidance: The source is recorded, or the figure is left blank and is not treated as final until advice is received.

fields.label: Cash buffer
fields.prompt: Enter the number of months of total fixed costs to hold in reserve, and where the reserve is kept.
fields.guidance: A whole or decimal number of months, with the location of the reserve written beside it.

fields.label: Monthly income target
fields.prompt: Add personal costs, business costs, the set-aside and the buffer contribution.
fields.guidance: The total matches the sum of the earlier fields and shows the buffer contribution separately.

fields.label: Average job value
fields.prompt: Enter the average amount invoiced per job over the last three months, or an estimate marked as an estimate.
fields.guidance: The basis is stated: actual invoices, or a labelled estimate.

fields.label: Materials and travel per job
fields.prompt: Enter the average materials and travel cost per job, from records or a labelled estimate.
fields.guidance: Covers only the costs that change with each job.

fields.label: Contribution per job
fields.prompt: Subtract materials and travel per job from the average job value.
fields.guidance: Equals average job value minus materials and travel per job.

fields.label: Break-even jobs per month
fields.prompt: Divide the monthly income target by the contribution per job, and round up to a whole job.
fields.guidance: The calculation is shown next to the result.

fields.label: Hours check
fields.prompt: Rows: hours per job; jobs per week; billable hours per week; non-billable hours per week (travel, quoting, admin, rework); total hours needed; hours available per week; fits (yes or no).
fields.guidance: Total hours needed must not exceed hours available. The calculation is visible.

fields.label: Decision taken after the hours check
fields.prompt: Name the change you chose (price, volume, cost or target), the reason and the date. If you chose no change, explain why the plan fits.
fields.guidance: One option is recorded, with a reason and a date.

fields.label: Review date
fields.prompt: Enter the date you will review the figures.
fields.guidance: A date within the next review cycle.

fields.label: Checklist: costs and hours confirmed
fields.prompt: Tick each item when it is done.
fields.guidance: Personal costs listed; business costs listed; set-aside source recorded or left blank; non-billable hours included; decision recorded.

levels.meets: Personal costs, business costs and the set-aside are listed separately, each with a total and a basis.
levels.does_not_meet: Costs are combined into one list, or a category is missing without a reason.

levels.meets: Break-even jobs are calculated from average job value minus materials and travel, with the calculation visible.
levels.does_not_meet: Break-even is calculated from gross job value, or the calculation cannot be followed.

levels.meets: Total hours needed, including travel, quoting, admin and rework, is compared with hours available, and the result is stated.
levels.does_not_meet: Only billable hours are counted, or the fit is not stated.

levels.meets: A single change, or a stated reason for no change, is recorded with a date.
levels.does_not_meet: No decision is recorded, or several options are listed without a choice.

levels.meets: Every tax, insurance or obligation figure has a source, or is left blank and not treated as final.
levels.does_not_meet: An unsourced obligation figure is presented as final.
